figures.alt: Diagram comparing two five-step pipelines: Palladio's treatise and shape grammar, ending in licence as motivated deviation, and a generative AI model, ending in fluctuation without a cause.
figures.caption: Fig. 1. Treatise and generative model: two pipelines compared. The analogy breaks down at the declared cause of variation. Graphic elaboration by the author.

figures.alt: Five schematic plans showing a villa derived step by step on a 5 x 3 grid: grid, central axis and hall, rooms, walls and openings, and a front loggia with columns.
figures.caption: Fig. 2. Schematic derivation of a plan on a 5 × 3 grid following the generative logic of the Palladian Grammar. Original teaching diagram by the author.

figures.alt: Three nested ellipses: the historical corpus of Palladio's villas inside the generative language of the grammar, inside the wider design space of all possible configurations.
figures.caption: Fig. 3. Historical corpus, generative language and design space. Graphic elaboration by the author based on data from Stiny and Mitchell (1978b) and Benrós et al. (2012).

figures.alt: Page 50 of Book II of Palladio's Quattro Libri: woodcut plan and front elevation of Villa Foscari, La Malcontenta, with its raised Ionic portico, below the original Italian text.
figures.caption: Fig. 4. A. Palladio, Villa Foscari (“La Malcontenta”), plan and elevation, I quattro libri dell’architettura, Book II, p. 50. Getty Research Institute (public domain).

figures.alt: Five cards listing a critical protocol for generative systems: provenance, rule, measure, deviation and responsibility, above a sequence describing a pedagogical inversion.
figures.caption: Fig. 5. The five-criterion critical protocol and the sequence of the pedagogical inversion. Graphic elaboration by the author.
